changelog.change: Initial entry — a genuine content gap (NIHSS existed but its usual thrombectomy-decision companion did not). Additive engine: each of the 10 standard regions scores 1 point if normal, summing to the conventional 0-10 ASPECTS value. Interpretation notes the 2023 large-core trials (SELECT2, ANGEL-ASPECT, and TENSION) that extended thrombectomy benefit below the traditional ASPECTS ≥6 cutoff.

purpose: Quantifies early ischemic change on non-contrast CT across 10 standard MCA-territory regions — used alongside NIHSS in thrombectomy eligibility and to estimate infarct-core extent.

items.label: M2 — MCA cortex lateral to the insular ribbon
M4 — anterior MCA territory, immediately superior to M1
M5 — lateral MCA territory, immediately superior to M2
M6 — posterior MCA territory, immediately superior to M3

interpretation.label: 8-9 — small core
interpretation.risk: Standard eligibility considerations for thrombolysis/thrombectomy apply

interpretation.label: 6-7 — moderate core
interpretation.risk: The traditional ASPECTS ≥ 6 thrombectomy-eligibility threshold; outcomes worsen as the score falls toward 6

interpretation.label: ≤ 5 — large core
interpretation.risk: Historically a relative exclusion for reperfusion therapy, but SELECT2, ANGEL-ASPECT, and TENSION (2023) all showed a thrombectomy benefit even in this range in appropriately selected patients — ASPECTS ≤ 5 is no longer an automatic exclusion; involve the stroke/neurointervention team rather than withholding on the score alone

notes: Score the hemisphere with the suspected infarct on the earliest available non-contrast CT (or DWI-ASPECTS on MRI, scored the same way). Each of the 10 regions starts credited as normal (1 point); mark 'early ischemic change' for hypoattenuation, loss of gray-white differentiation, or focal swelling — the score is 10 minus the number of abnormal regions, not a severity-graded per-region score. Caudate/lentiform/internal-capsule/insular-ribbon changes carry more weight for functional outcome than an equivalent M-region change, but the standard score treats all 10 regions equally; this tool implements the standard (unweighted) ASPECTS as published, which is what's used in trial eligibility criteria and most stroke protocols.
buildNote: Additive engine models the conventional 0-10 score directly (1 point per normal region) rather than a 'deficit' formula, so the number shown to the user matches what every stroke protocol and trial publication reports. Pairs with nihss (already built) in thrombectomy decision-making — cross-referenced via aliases/keywords rather than a `related` field, since the calculator schema doesn't carry one.
